applicableAreas: Southern property boundary adjacent to overhead electric line
findings.comment: Large trees (mature height 40+ feet per ECM Appendix F) including Cedar Elm (10 trees at 4-inch caliper) and Live Oak (2 trees at 4-inch caliper) are proposed along the southern property boundary at approximately 4.2 feet from the overhead electric distribution conductor. This distance is significantly less than the required 25-foot minimum clearance for large trees from distribution conductors. Measured distance: 4.2 feet (medium confidence). No documented written approval from Austin Energy for this clearance variance is provided.

applicableAreas: Northwest corner area near Building 1, adjacent to underground electric line
findings.comment: Proposed trees are located approximately 9.7 feet from underground electric infrastructure in the northwest corner. While this exceeds the 5-foot prohibition distance for trees directly above underground equipment, it falls within the 20-foot zone requiring root barriers (minimum 4 feet deep, positioned 5 feet from equipment). No root barrier specifications or details are provided on the landscape plan or in the landscape details to demonstrate compliance with root barrier requirements.

applicableAreas: Southern property boundary and throughout site where large trees are proposed
findings.comment: Large trees (40+ foot mature height per ECM Appendix F) including Cedar Elm and Live Oak are identified in the plant schedule on Sheet 35 with specific sizes (4-inch caliper, 16-foot target height). However, these large trees are not differentiated on the landscape plan itself with callouts, symbols, or height/size annotations. The landscape plan shows tree locations with generic symbols without distinguishing large trees (40+ feet) from smaller trees, preventing visual verification of large tree clearances from overhead facilities.

applicableAreas: Entire site including overhead and underground electric infrastructure
findings.comment: The landscape plan shows the overhead electric line (labeled OHE) along the southern and western property boundaries, but the specific voltage classification (distribution vs. transmission) is not labeled or noted. Additionally, the exact position of the outer conductor versus the pole centerline is not dimensioned or clearly distinguished on the landscape plan, making it difficult to verify clearance compliance. The underground electric line in the northwest is similarly shown without clear callouts for specific equipment locations.

applicableAreas: Southern property boundary adjacent to overhead electric line; possibly other restricted clearance zones
findings.comment: Large trees are proposed within the prohibited clearance zone (4.2 feet from the overhead distribution conductor, requiring 25 feet minimum for large trees). No documented written approval from Austin Energy authorizing this variance is provided in the submitted site plan or supplementary documents. The Master Comment Report references Electric Review comments from Austin Energy via Bluebeam link, but no formal approval letter or variance authorization is attached to the application.
